units.leftText: Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother,
units.rightText: Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, to Philemon our beloved and fellow-worker,

units.leftText: to Apphia our sister, to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church that meets at your house:
units.rightText: and to Apphia our sister, and to Archippus our fellow-soldier, and to the church in thy house:
leftNotes: 1:2 You and Your are singular throughout this letter, except in verses 3, 22, and 25.

units.leftText: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Philemon’s Faith and Love
units.rightText: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: I always thank my God, remembering you in my prayers,
units.rightText: I thank my God always, making mention of thee in my prayers,

units.leftText: because I hear about your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all the saints.
units.rightText: hearing of thy love, and of the faith which thou hast toward the Lord Jesus, and toward all the saints;

units.leftText: I pray that your partnership in the faith may become effective as you fully acknowledge every good thing that is ours in Christ.
units.rightText: that the fellowship of thy faith may become effectual, in the knowledge of every good thing which is in you, unto Christ.

units.leftText: I take great joy and encouragement in your love, because you, brother, have refreshed the hearts of the saints. Paul’s Appeal for Onesimus
units.rightText: For I had much joy and comfort in thy love, because the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through thee, brother.

units.leftText: So although in Christ I am bold enough to order you to do what is proper,
units.rightText: Wherefore, though I have all boldness in Christ to enjoin thee that which is befitting,

units.leftText: I prefer to appeal on the basis of love. For I, Paul, am now aged, and a prisoner of Christ Jesus as well.
units.rightText: yet for love’s sake I rather beseech, being such a one as Paul the aged, and now a prisoner also of Christ Jesus:

units.leftText: I appeal to you for my child Onesimus, whose father I became while I was in chains.
units.rightText: I beseech thee for my child, whom I have begotten in my bonds, Onesimus,
leftNotes: 1:10 Onesimus means useful (see verse 11) or beneficial (see verse 20).

units.leftText: Formerly he was useless to you, but now he has become useful both to you and to me.
units.rightText: who once was unprofitable to thee, but now is profitable to thee and to me:

units.leftText: I am sending back to you him who is my very heart.
units.rightText: whom I have sent back to thee in his own person, that is, my very heart:

units.leftText: I would have liked to keep him with me, so that on your behalf he could minister to me in my chains for the gospel.
units.rightText: whom I would fain have kept with me, that in thy behalf he might minister unto me in the bonds of the gospel:

units.leftText: But I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your goodness will not be out of compulsion, but by your own free will.
units.rightText: but without thy mind I would do nothing; that thy goodness should not be as of necessity, but of free will.

units.leftText: For perhaps this is why he was separated from you for a while, so that you might have him back for good —
units.rightText: For perhaps he was therefore parted from thee for a season, that thou shouldest have him for ever;

units.leftText: no longer as a slave, but better than a slave, as a beloved brother. He is especially beloved to me, but even more so to you, both in person and in the Lord.
units.rightText: no longer as a servant, but more than a servant, a brother beloved, specially to me, but how much rather to thee, both in the flesh and in the Lord.

units.leftText: So if you consider me a partner, receive him as you would receive me.
units.rightText: If then thou countest me a partner, receive him as myself.

units.leftText: But if he has wronged you in any way or owes you anything, charge it to my account.
units.rightText: But if he hath wronged thee at all, or oweth thee aught, put that to mine account;

units.leftText: I, Paul, write this with my own hand. I will repay it— not to mention that you owe me your very self.
units.rightText: I Paul write it with mine own hand, I will repay it: that I say not unto thee that thou owest to me even thine own self besides.

units.leftText: Yes, brother, let me have some benefit from you in the Lord. Refresh my heart in Christ.
units.rightText: Yea, brother, let me have joy of thee in the Lord: refresh my heart in Christ.
leftNotes: 1:20 Greek onaimēn, a play on the name Onesimus

units.leftText: Confident of your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even more than I ask.
units.rightText: Having confidence in thine obedience I write unto thee, knowing that thou wilt do even beyond what I say.

units.leftText: In the meantime, prepare a guest room for me, because I hope that through your prayers I will be restored to you. Additional Greetings
units.rightText: But withal prepare me also a lodging: for I hope that through your prayers I shall be granted unto you.

units.leftText: Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, sends you greetings,
units.rightText: Epaphras, my fellow-prisoner in Christ Jesus, saluteth thee;

units.leftText: as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow workers.
units.rightText: and so do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, Luke, my fellow-workers.

units.leftText: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
units.rightText: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
